title: Neiko 01408A Electronic Digital Caliper with Extra Large LCD Screen $34.73 (RRP $67.49) + Delivery @ Amazon US via AU
body:
Deal: Neiko 01408A Electronic Digital Caliper with Extra Large LCD Screen $34.73 (RRP $67.49) + Delivery @ Amazon US via AU

[Tuttle] Have one from Aldi, but annoyingly you have to be very careful when expanding it out, as the measurement can be out if you're too quick or abrupt.
And since one is using it for precision, even a few mms matter.
Does this avoid that issue?
- I ask as this looks identical.to the Aldi special buys one.
[Beetleeater] If your tolerance is "a few mm" this will be good. If your tolerance is in microns, i'd buy the mitutoyo.
Avoid your abrupt issue completely = measure twice.
[bamzero] These are probably 50mm longer than the Aldi ones I'm guessing you got.
I would hope based on rep they are better than the Aldi ones but haven't tried them myself (the Neiko, I did have Aldi ones). Mitutoyo is the go to high end ones but there are plenty of fakes out there, not sure if Neiko gets targeted the same way.
I got these which are still noname but I was actually kinda impressed with them. Still 150mm but build quality feels much better than the Aldi ones, pretty smooth action (and all metal casing so feels nice and weighty). Accuracy is with 0.02mm of my old dial calipers as far as I can tell. Thing with calipers is accuracy is always going to vary just based on how much pressure you apply. If you are getting discrepancy on the left side of the decimal point though, chuck em out.
[tonyamazing] My aldi one would constantly be out. I bought this cheapo one to replace it.
https://amzn.asia/d/07lWvz9E
Moving it around super quick it's never "off". As in, when fully closed its back to 0, as expected. Not like the aldi one where fully closed was often less than 0.
[user6598123549] i got ones from Ali they are absolute trash not worth even $3
[fantombloo] What do you think is trashy about them? (I have a bunch of them lying around and find them fine.)
[kmp] I can recommend SHANE branded calliper on Ali. It's no Mitutoyo, but it has good reviews and seems pretty accurate.
[bamzero] Hmm, no free shipping for Prime? Checking on Amazon.com seems to be shipped and sold by Amazon not 3rd party too.
(Side note, noticed if you're logged in Amazon.com is now providing their own price history of sorts via Alexa AI.)
[freddofrog42] These are fine for most domestic purposes and can be used without a battery - they're generic and I have at least 3 kicking around and ALL were much cheaper than this version. I've even got a couple of 100% plastic ones sans display from SCA which cost $0.99 and if you you know how to read them they're again fine for domestic purposes.
For actual machining accuracy forget it. You will need an accurate tool and a good machinist - sadly the latter is getting increasing rare as the oldies retire etc.
[slipperypete] Yeah, there are a lot of generic ones around that look very similar. I got one for my old workplace from Bunnings for around $40 and it is quite awful, poor feel, buttons are flimsy and it has play in it. I tried this one a while back and really liked it. I've had it on a price watch for about 8 months now, and this is a big drop. If I only had one, I would get the Mitutoyo. I guess I am posting this for people who want something with a digital readout. It takes all of two minutes to learn how to use an analogue one properly, but sometimes a quick measure is good enough.It definitely is a bit more quality than some of the generic versions I've seen though and has good reviews.
[bread69] I recommend my apprentices purchase mitutoyo 300mm analog verniers 530-119 or something alike they last forever otherwise they usually cheap on out on something from bunnings
the thing is with these cheap verniers the scales cant keep up with movement and if you arent measuring alot they can skip and measure something wrong
someone with a trained eye or knowledge will know apprentices wont catch it
digital mitutoyo verniers are nice to haves they were recently $320 from bolts and industrial but they are pretty much 1 drop and your internal measurments become unreliable and need micrometers anyway so thats why i recommend 530-119 to apprentices now
dial verniers are a fools trap dont buy them swarf will jam the gear up eventually and write them off
[slipperypete] good points. i prefer my non digital. the cheapo ones feel spongey. this one didn't feel bad at all but constant use may be telling.
what is your work? just curious, the 300mm are quite big….I can def see the cheaper digital ones skipping at those larger distances
[bread69] @slipperypete: fitter and machinist in mining
[bwad] I really wish someone made a left hand version of this
[MS Paint] You can buy left handed vernier calipers
[MS Paint] Not sure if this is a bargain but more to prove that they exist
[Meteor Anarcom] I got one for something close to 2 dollars on AliExpress
[banana365] You can buy a Little Tikes Cosy Coupe for less than 1% of the price of a Camry.
[Lizard Spock] A girth of >20cm is a medical condition, not a flex.
[tangcla] Wouldn't these be a better buy? Reviews seem positive. https://amzn.asia/d/0fVhiKoK
[bulletbill88] Looks very similar to generic digital one? Have one, not particularly accurate and the screen goes in and out. Mitutoyo analogue one on the other hand will never need replacing.
[Dollarsandsense] As a professional user of these devices for Sheetmetal manufacturing where accuracy to 0.1mm matters the kinchrome ones from Bunnings are really good. We have 5 of them floating around our workshop, they are currently $146 but am sure we paid a fair bit less than this a few months ago..
https://www.bunnings.com.au/kincrome-150mm-digital-vernier_p…
[YouWillOwnNothingAnd] If you're looking for decent stainless calipers at a good price, available in smaller and larger sizes then Hare and Forbes are the go.
[bread69] I can confirm that hare and forbes branded equipment are mainly rebadged aliexpress/alibaba stuff
[YouWillOwnNothingAnd] Fair enough, if you can find the equivalent fit and finish on Aliexpress for a significantly cheaper price then I'll buy it.
[bread69] alot of their stuff is just rebadged aliexpress stuff their micrometer sets are particularly easy to compare if you want a set they just change the box and logo
I got nothing against aliexpress just dont pay more than you need to
[syme321] Ideal for precision bread cutting!
Ref: German bread cutter
https://www.instagram.com/germanbreadcutter?igsh=b2ZqaDZoOHp…
[Reiai] Is there a semi-reliable accessory that anyone can recommend to measure specific points? Something that would clip on to the jaws, have two narrow points attached, and be sturdy enough to give consistent results after zeroing.
[Hornpub] for cheap ones, i always go for the vernier version. no need to worry about battery and inconsistent measure. Pure mechanical always works.
